captions.instagram:
How is makhan made?

Makhan is not squeezed out of milk. It is milk fat turned inside out. Billions of tiny fat globules float in water, each in its own skin, until the mathani tears the skins and the fat sticks together. Churn a pot, watch the globules, and see why ice goes in on a hot day.

→ Milk hides its fat as billions of tiny globules, each wrapped in its own skin.
→ Left alone, the fat floats up by about a millimetre an hour. That layer on top is cream.
→ In 1878 Gustaf de Laval patented the spinning separator: thousands of g, and cream in seconds.
→ The mathani: a rope wound on a rod. Pull right and it spins one way, pull left and it spins back.
→ Churning whips in air. Fat globules crowd onto the bubbles, their skins tear, and liquid fat glues them into clumps.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/butterclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How is makhan made? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Makhan is not squeezed out of milk. It is milk fat turned inside out. Billions of tiny fat globules float in water, each in its own skin, until the mathani tears the skins and the fat sticks together. Churn a pot, watch the globules, and see why ice goes in on a hot day.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/butterclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/butterclear

In this video:
• Milk hides its fat. Milk is about 87% water.
• Cream rises by Stokes' law. Fat is lighter than the watery milk, so globules float up at about a millimetre an hour, and bigger ones rise much faster.
• The churn goes back and forth. A mathani is a rod spun by a rope: pull one end and it turns one way, pull the other and it turns back.
• The break is an emulsion flipping. Globules crowd onto air bubbles, their skins tear, and liquid fat glues them into clumps.
• Wash, work, salt. Washing removes buttermilk, and working presses the leftover water into droplets too small to see.
• Hard cold, soft warm. Milk fat is hundreds of fats with different melting points, so butter has a melting range.
